interface.title: E2P Simulator (Effect-to-Prediction Simulator) v1.3.0
interface.field: Behavioural, biomedical and psychiatric research methods: biomarker and individual-differences studies, diagnostic tool validation, predictive modelling
interface.stage_of_work: Study planning, and interpreting results after a study
interface.what_it_is_for: Turns an effect size (Cohen's d, odds ratio, Pearson's r and others), measurement reliability and outcome base rate into the classification performance you can expect (ROC/PR curves, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, net benefit), and also gives multi-predictor, calibration-transfer and sample-size estimates.

data.note: All results are computed from parameters typed or set with sliders. Nothing is uploaded or loaded. The scatter plot in Continuous mode is drawn from simulated points. Built-in defaults are d = 1.34, ICC = 0.5, κ = 0.5, base rate 45% in Binary mode and r = 0.5 in Continuous mode.

tree.general: Translate an effect-size statistic into expected real-world predictive performance, and plan studies around that
tree.specific: Use E2P Simulator to go from d, OR or r plus ICC, κ and base rate to ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, PPV, NPV, net benefit, calibration and required N

features.name: Linked effect-size converter table with true and observed columns
features.general: Enter an effect in any of several equivalent statistics and see every other statistic update, both before and after correction for measurement error
features.specific: Typing in the True column for Cohen's d, U3, Odds Ratio, Log OR, point-biserial r or η² (Binary), or Pearson's r and R² (Continuous), recomputes the rest. The Obs. column shows the values attenuated by ICC and κ and does not take input. A slider above the table moves the effect size continuously
steps: Type a value into any True field (for example OR 2.5)
Read the converted d, U3, r and so on
Read the Obs. column after attenuation
Drag the effect-size slider to scan values
serves_tasks: Turn a group-difference effect into classification performance
Turn a correlation with a graded outcome into classification performance
Find the effect size needed for a target discrimination

features.name: Reliability attenuation controls
features.general: Set how reliable each measure is and see how much of the true effect survives
features.specific: Sliders and number fields for ICC1, ICC2 and κ (Binary) or ICCx and ICCy (Continuous). They drive d_obs = d_true·√(2·ICC1·ICC2/(ICC1+ICC2))·sin(π/2·κ) and r_obs = r_true·√(ICCx·ICCy)
steps: Set ICC for the predictor in each group (or ICCx)
Set outcome reliability κ (or ICCy)
Read the observed effect and the attenuated AUC
serves_tasks: Lower the reliability of one measure and read the attenuated effect
Compare performance with perfect measurement against what is actually observed (group-difference outcome)
Compare performance with perfect measurement against what is actually observed (graded outcome)

features.name: Draggable cutoff on the distribution plot, linked to ROC/PR markers and a metrics panel
features.general: Move a decision threshold across two overlapping score distributions and see the operating point and confusion-matrix metrics update
features.specific: Drag the red cutoff line, or type the threshold probability pt. The red dots move along the ROC and PR curves. Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, BA, PPV, NPV, F1 and MCC update, and Show more metrics adds LR±, DOR, G-Mean, J and κ. Caution: in the replay (ICC1 0.3), dragging the line right lowered pt and gave below-chance metrics, so values on that side look wrong and should be checked against a typed pt
steps: Drag the red line on the predictor distribution plot (or type pt)
Watch the operating-point dots move on the ROC and PR curves
Read the metrics panel
Optionally press Show more metrics
serves_tasks: Move the cutoff and read the trade-off between sensitivity and specificity, with the full set of metrics

features.name: Decision curve with net benefit gain
features.general: Compare the net benefit of acting on the predictor with treating everyone or no one, across risk thresholds
features.specific: Decision Curve Analysis plot with Treat All (dashed) and Treat None (dotted) reference lines. A red marker sits at the current pt (set through the cutoff controls of f3), and ΔNB reports the gain over the better reference strategy. Clicking the curve does not set pt
steps: Set the base rate
Set pt with the threshold field
Read ΔNB and where the curve sits above the All and None lines
serves_tasks: Set the threshold to a stated risk tolerance and read the net benefit

features.name: True/Observed view toggle
features.general: Switch every plot and metric between the error-free and the measured scenario
features.specific: The True | Observed button pair at the top right of the main plot redraws the distributions, ROC/PR and decision curves and the metrics for the true or the reliability-attenuated effect
steps: Press True
Read the AUC and ΔNB
Press Observed
Compare

features.name: Binary/Continuous outcome mode switch
features.general: Choose whether the outcome is a two-class label or a graded score that gets split at a base-rate cutoff
features.specific: A page-wide setting rather than a single widget: the Binary / Continuous toggle swaps the single-predictor panel (distributions, or a scatter plot of simulated points split at the base rate), changes the multi-predictor calculator (Mahalanobis D or multiple R²) and the sample-size criteria, and hides the Calibration module in Continuous mode
steps: Press Continuous
Enter Pearson's r, ICCx, ICCy and base rate
Read the scatter plot, the group distributions and the derived d and OR
serves_tasks: Turn a correlation with a graded outcome into classification performance

features.name: Multi-predictor performance curve with recordable comparison curves
features.general: Plot combined performance against the number of predictors under stated effect size and collinearity, with a target line, and freeze curves to compare scenarios
features.specific: From Single to Multiple Predictors: set Target ROC-AUC (or Target R²), base rate, per-predictor d (or r), collinearity ρ and maximum p. The ROC-AUC (or R²) and PR-AUC against number-of-predictors plots show dashed target lines. Record curve freezes the current curve, hovering a point shows its value, and Reset restores the defaults and clears recorded curves
steps: Set the target and base rate
Set per-predictor effect and collinearity
Press Record curve
Change a parameter and compare the live curve with the recorded one
Hover a point to read the p at which the target is met
Press Reset
serves_tasks: Estimate how many correlated predictors are needed to reach a target performance

features.name: Development-to-target calibration transfer
features.general: Specify the conditions where a model was built and where it will be used, then see the resulting calibration curve and calibration statistics
features.specific: Two parameter panels (Development and Target population: true d, ICC1, ICC2, κ, base rate), each with its own distribution plot and ROC/PR-AUC. A calibration plot of predicted against observed frequency is drawn next to a perfect-calibration line, with Brier, ICI, slope and intercept. A draggable cutoff moves in both plots and moves a marker along the calibration curve. Supported by screens only; not replayed
steps: Set the development population parameters
Set the target population base rate and/or reliability
Read the calibration curve and slope, intercept, Brier and ICI
Drag the cutoff to inspect calibration at a given predicted risk
serves_tasks: See how a different prevalence in the new population biases predicted risks
See how noisier measurement in the new population distorts predicted risks

features.name: Multi-criterion sample-size calculator
features.general: Compute the minimum N for a prediction model under several published criteria, take the largest, and plot each criterion against the number of parameters
features.specific: Binary mode criteria: EPV rule of thumb, outcome-proportion precision (margin m), MAPE (δ), shrinkage (Cox–Snell R², S) and Nagelkerke R² optimism. Continuous mode criteria: residual-SD precision, shrinkage (anticipated R², S) and R² optimism (δ). The largest value is reported as Required Sample Size, with the binding criterion highlighted, and a line chart of N against p is drawn for every criterion
steps: Set predictor parameters p and the base rate
Adjust each criterion's inputs (EPV, m, δ, R², S)
Read the required N and which criterion binds
Compare the criteria in the N-versus-p chart
serves_tasks: Sample size for a binary-outcome model
Sample size for a continuous-outcome model
